title: Terrain is opaque underfoot — no translucent ground at the player’s feet
note: The walkable ground is opaque with depth writing on; a milky floor shows within two seconds of walking.
intent: One run shipped a marsh whose water plane read as a milky semi-transparent floor at the player’s feet — visible within two seconds of walking, invisible in every registered camera because all of them framed from waist height or above and none looked down. The ground the player stands on is an opaque MeshStandardMaterial (transparent false, opacity 1, depthWrite true); any water or mist plane is a separate tagged object at its own height that never doubles as the floor, and the floor sits 2–3 stops brighter than the figures on it so silhouettes separate (near-black floors only in the dark-interior case). Buried props intersect the ground by ≥ 30% of their height with a displaced ring at the contact perimeter so they read as buried rather than sitting on it, and every noise displacement clamps UVs to [0,1] and guards against NaN before it reaches a geometry. Verify from a player-eye camera pitched 25–30° down, never only from a vista.

check.note: The walkable ground is opaque (transparent false, opacity 1, depthWrite true); a milky semi-transparent floor at the player feet hides from vista cameras and shows within two seconds of walking.

port: The ground/terrain facet owns makeTerrain() and bury() (the substrate and its drifts are one material system); tag the walkable mesh "terrain" and any marsh plane "water", never both on one object, and register a player-eye camera on walkable ground so the floor is in every iteration’s evidence.

evidence.note: the judge must see what the player sees: a milky semi-transparent floor at the feet was invisible in every registered camera; add a player-eye camera pitched 25–30° down
buried objects intersect the ground by ≥30% of their height with a displaced ring; floor 2–3 stops brighter than the figures; clamp UVs before noise, guard NaN before geometry
material systems are atomic: base surface, its displacement and drifts are one facet
